newsitem.title: GERMANY: More strikes to hit allied army bases in Germany.
newsitem.headline: More strikes to hit allied army bases in Germany.

text.p: German civilian workers at allied army bases in Germany will restart strike action on Tuesday after the collapse of talks over cost-cutting measures by their employers, unions said on Monday.

The OeTV public sector and DAG white-collar workers' unions said that despite negotiations it was clear the army bases, mainly American, were determined to push ahead with plans to reduce the number of civilians they employ.
Around 35,000 civilians, mostly German, are employed by the allies across the country. An earlier six-week strike involved some 3,000 workers.

"While job protection measures are being discussed at the negotiating table, the U.S. army forces want to get the matter over and done with and kick their staff out on to the street," the OeTV said in a statement.
It said it drew this conclusion from a questionnaire handed to some 6,500 staff by the U.S. army base management relating to possible compensation measures.
Many civilians employed at the bases have already seen their jobs go as army forces in Germany have been reduced since the end of the Cold War.
